source.title: Armagh Guardian, 3 June 1927, p. 3 (list of the new county council: "Returned Unopposed" and "Retiring Councillors deemed to be re-elected"); nominations from the Newry Reporter, 28 April 1927, p. 6 ("County Elections: Nominations in Armagh")
source.publisher: Armagh Guardian (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: every name checked against the two page images; returned unopposed, no poll

note: Triennial election of the county council, 1927: nominations received by Thomas E. Reid, secretary, 26 April 1927; the only poll was in Portadown, 26 May 1927. No party labels are printed for the unopposed members in the nominations or the list of the new council, so none are given. Returned unopposed. William James Gibson: no party label printed in 1927. At other elections he stood as Unionist (Poyntzpass, 29 May 1924, printed 'U': Lurgan Mail, 7 June 1924, p. 7 ("Co. Armagh Election Results"); nominations and labels from the Frontier Sentinel, 10 May 1924, p. 5; Poyntzpass, 29 May 1930, printed 'U': Belfast News-Letter, 30 April 1930, p. 15 ("Apathy in Rural Districts"); withdrawals from the Lurgan Mail, 10 May 1930, p. 4 ("No Contests in Armagh: County Council Nominees Withdraw")).
